This tests a different block granularity, not T1-style whole-buffer validation. Catalog evidence is mixed: the selected 16-byte repeated-scan parent measured 60.43 µs, while a distinct one-way 16-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix program measured 39.98 µs against the 49.62 µs baseline. Whether 32-byte scans help the official mixed-width n=65536 workload remains unmeasured.

retained: Changed the repeated ASCII scan from one 16-byte vector per iteration to two adjacent 16-byte vectors checked together; scan only when at least 32 bytes remain.
Skip a 32-byte block only when the OR-combined vectors have no high bits. Otherwise leave the index unchanged for scalar scanning and strict decoding from the known boundary.
Retained bounded scalar tail handling, UTF-8 validity rules, ABI, output, and thread budget.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: A repeated 32-byte SSE2 ASCII-skip hybrid may reduce scan-loop overhead relative to the selected parent's 16-byte scan while retaining scalar UTF-8 decoding. This tests a different block granularity, not T1-style whole-buffer validation. Catalog evidence is mixed: the selected 16-byte repeated-scan parent measured 60.43 µs, while a distinct one-way 16-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix program measured 39.98 µs against the 49.62 µs baseline. Whether 32-byte scans help the official mixed-width n=65536 workload remains unmeasured.

retained: Changed the repeated ASCII scan from one 16-byte vector per iteration to two adjacent 16-byte vectors checked together; scan only when at least 32 bytes remain.
Skip a 32-byte block only when the OR-combined vectors have no high bits. Otherwise leave the index unchanged for scalar scanning and strict decoding from the known boundary.
Retained bounded scalar tail handling, UTF-8 validity rules, ABI, output, and thread budget.

mission.hypothesis: A one-way SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid using bounded 64-byte ASCII blocks may amortize scan overhead versus the earlier 16-byte prefix hybrid. It skips a block only when all four SSE2 vectors are ASCII; otherwise the strict scalar decoder resumes at that block's known code-point boundary and validates the first high-bit byte rather than assuming it is a lead. Whether this granularity helps the official mixed-width n=65536 workload is unmeasured.

retained: Replace repeated SIMD scans between decoded code points with a single bounded scan over complete 64-byte prefix blocks, each checked by four unaligned SSE2 loads.
Skip a 64-byte block only when all bytes are ASCII; otherwise leave the index at the block start for strict scalar validation of the suffix, including any leading ASCII and the first high-bit byte.

The official mixed-width n=65536 workload must determine whether larger blocks help or merely add overhead.

retained: Added a compile-time-guarded SSE2 scan that loads four 16-byte vectors only when at least 64 bytes remain, combines them to test whether the full 64-byte block is ASCII, and skips the block only when every byte is ASCII.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: A compile-time-guarded SSE2 scan can skip complete 16-byte ASCII blocks before the existing scalar UTF-8 decoder handles non-ASCII bytes. This may reduce per-byte work on long ASCII spans, but the benefit depends on the official mixed-width input; the first high-bit byte remains for scalar validation. The baseline is valid at 49.623 µs mean, but no candidate speedup is established.

retained: Added a compile-time-guarded SSE2 high-bit scan that advances across full 16-byte ASCII blocks only; scalar scanning handles tails and the first block containing a high-bit byte before the unchanged strict decoder validates it.
